subject: Re: Northshore pilot — scope, success KPIs and next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@northshore.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Northshore pilot — proposed success slate and next steps

Hi Samir / Ayesha —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on the problem space and the sample flows. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture a concise pilot plan with measurable gates so we can lock scope and get procurement moving. Below is a proposed 4-week pilot (one sprint) with owners and KPIs. Please review and flag anything missing.

Summary (high level)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Northshore’s document-classification & summarization flows at production-like scale; measure latency, throughput, cost/token, and quality vs baseline.
- Length: 4 weeks (pilot), with a short smoke validation in week 0.
- Success gates: operational (telemetry + stability), performance (latency/throughput), cost targets, and quality thresholds on a representative eval set.

Proposed success criteria (quantitative)
- Latency: p50 < 120ms and p95 < 450ms for typical request length (avg 180 tokens, max 600 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 45 requests/sec (concurrent 30 clients) with <1% error rate.
- Cost: average inference cost <= $0.0035 per token (model + infra optimized).
- Quality: classification accuracy >= 90% and summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.38 on the agreed evaluation dataset; hallucination rate < 2% (as measured by our shared rubric).

Operational/measurement details
- Data: Northshore provides a 1.5k example eval set with labels + a 500-sample blind set for final scoring.
- Telemetry: we will provide a metrics dashboard (token breakdown, p50/p95, error codes) and a short tracing hook to sample requests for QA.
- Owners: Redwood PM (Rishi) for delivery/coordination; Monica (CS) for onboarding, telemetry, and runbook; Lauren (Solutions) for prompt engineering and evaluation definitions.

Timeline & next steps
1) Week 0 (smoke): shared samples + baseline run (2–3 days).
2) Week 1: baseline vs Redwood model variants; initial tuning and caching policy.
3) Week 2–3: load testing to reach throughput targets; iterate prompts and quantization profile.
4) Week 4: final scoring on blind set, wrap doc, decision meeting.

Immediate asks for Northshore
- Share the 1.5k labeled eval set + blind set (S3 or shared Drive link).
- Confirm any regulator-required redaction rules for logs.
- Indicate approval to proceed with the proposed pilot timeline so we can send a light SOW and kickoff calendar invite.

Attachments: I attached a short pilot template and our standard SLA matrix for reference — these are draft and can be pared down for a short pilot.

Thanks — I’ll add the shared links and a first cut SOW once you confirm scope.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — this looks sensible and much clearer than our notes from the call. A few quick items:

- The eval set is ready; I’ll upload to an S3 bucket and share links by EOD tomorrow (S3 link + access keys).
- For latency, our internal SLA target is p95 < 600ms, so your p95 < 450ms target would be a nice uplift if achievable.
- On cost: we need a realistic estimate for the full-week steady-state token mix (we have a heavier tail of long docs; average token estimate may be closer to 240). Can you run cost projections for avg=180 and avg=240?
- Procurement will need a short SOW and a statement on data handling. We can start with your draft SOW.

We’re in favor of the 4-week cadence. Can Monica own the telemetry/workflow syncs? She worked our previous vendor onboarding and that went well.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML, Northshore AI

Samir —

Thanks — we’ll run the cost projection for average tokens 180/240 and include model-variant comparisons (fp16 vs qt8 quantized). Monica will own the telemetry sync — Monica, can you confirm available dashboards and the sample trace workflow?

Quick clarifications and refined gates (updated):
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms at avg=180 tokens; for avg=240 tokens p95 target relaxed to < 620ms.
- Throughput: 45 req/sec sustained; we’ll validate across 30–40 parallel clients.
- Cost: target <= $0.0035/token at avg=180; at avg=240 we’ll show delta and recommend an ops knob (batching/quantization) if delta > 12%.
- Quality: classification accuracy >= 90% on the labeled set; summarization benchmark will use the blind set and human spot-checking + ROUGE-L >= 0.38.

Next steps (immediate)
- Samir: share S3 eval link + any redaction requirements (EOD tomorrow).
- Redwood: deliver cost projection + a draft SOW and pilot-runbook by Friday (I’ll circulate).
- Schedule: proposed kickoff Mon Jun 23 (smoke + baseline).

Thanks — looping Ben to keep calendar/kit items ready for a quick demo.

Best,
Rishi

- Dashboard: token breakdown, p50/p95, error rate by endpoint, per-route throughput graphs (Grafana link sent at kickoff).
- Tracing: a sampling hook that returns a short trace id you can map back to the payload; we redact PII by default but will apply your redaction doc if you provide it.
- Runbook: an incident playbook for the pilot (who to call for incidents, escalation path, and fallback model variant).

Ownership & contacts
- Onboarding lead (telemetry & runbook): Monica Patel (monica@redwood.com)
- Prompt engineering & evaluation definitions: Lauren Bishop (lauren@redwood.com)
- Proof demo / infra readiness: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.com)

One operational ask: please confirm whether your security team requires a VPN connection or whether S3 presigned links + IP allowlisting is sufficient. If you need VPC peering, we’ll surface that in the SOW but it will add ~5 business days to the prep work.

I’ll follow up with the dashboard preview and a small checklist for onboarding (API keys, allowed IPs, sample payload format).

Cheers,
